name: Violin
shortDescription: Four-string bowed instrument producing continuous tone through rosin-coated horsehair bow friction.
description: The violin produces sound through stick-slip friction between the rosined bow hair and strings. The Helmholtz corner — a kink in the string's sawtooth wave — travels back and forth at the fundamental frequency. The bridge acts as a mechanical lever coupling this energy to the asymmetric top plate, creating complex radiation modes via the f-holes and the bass bar inside.
historicalOrigins: Emerged in 16th-century northern Italy (Cremona), perfected by luthiers Amati, Stradivari, and Guarneri del Gesù. The Stradivarius (1700–1725) remains the acoustic benchmark.
acousticPrinciples: Helmholtz stick-slip motion: bow hair alternately grips and slips string at fundamental frequency
Sawtooth wave from string contains all harmonic overtones (f, 2f, 3f...)
Bridge acts as mechanical filter and lever between string and top plate
F-holes provide air resonance coupling and tonal radiation

characteristics.timbralColor: Bright, singing, complex, capable of extreme dynamic nuance
characteristics.orchestralRole: Lead melodic voice, vibrato expressiveness, ensemble unison, solo virtuosity

soundDNA.exciter: Rosined horsehair bow creating stick-slip Helmholtz friction on steel/gut string
soundDNA.resonator: Spruce top plate, maple back/sides, internal bass bar, sound post
soundDNA.harmonics: Rich sawtooth harmonic series; bowing pressure controls spectral brightness
soundDNA.attackDecay: Continuous sustained tone (no decay while bowed); attack speed controlled by bow velocity
soundDNA.timbreProfile: Singing, bright, complex; vibrato adds pitch modulation for warmth
soundDNA.radiationPattern: Dipole from top/back plates with directional high-frequency radiation

body.label: Resonant Body
body.function: Hollow wooden body amplifies string vibration through complex plate and cavity resonances.

characteristics.material: Sitka Spruce top; European Maple back and sides
characteristics.mechanism: Dipole plate radiator with internal Helmholtz cavity

top_plate.label: Spruce Top Plate
top_plate.function: Primary radiation surface driven by bridge. Internal bass bar stiffens the treble side.

characteristics.material: Quarter-sawn Sitka or European Spruce with bass bar

f_holes.label: F-Holes
f_holes.function: Symmetrical apertures releasing internal air resonance and tonal radiation.

characteristics.mechanism: Helmholtz port resonance; air mass outlet

bridge.label: Maple Bridge
bridge.function: Precision-carved bridge mechanically couples string vibration to the top plate.

characteristics.material: Bosnian Maple with carved internal cutouts

strings.label: Violin Strings
strings.function: Four tuned strings (G-D-A-E) vibrating in Helmholtz stick-slip motion under bow.

characteristics.material: Steel core E, synthetic/gut G-D-A strings

fingerboard.label: Ebony Fingerboard
fingerboard.function: Unfretted ebony surface allowing continuous pitch glissando and vibrato.

characteristics.mechanism: Continuous pitch variation by finger pressure position

chinrest.label: Chinrest & Tailpiece
chinrest.function: Stabilises violin against chin; tailpiece anchors strings and fine-tuners.

characteristics.mechanism: String tension anchor with fine-tuner adjusters

scroll.label: Scroll & Pegbox
scroll.function: Ornamental scroll houses four friction pegs for coarse tuning.

characteristics.mechanism: Friction peg tuning; hand-pressure against pegbox walls

followTheSound.title: Stick-Slip Helmholtz Motion
followTheSound.explanation: Rosined bow hair grips and releases string at fundamental frequency, creating sawtooth wave.

followTheSound.title: Mechanical Coupling
followTheSound.explanation: Bridge transfers string energy with filtering — curved feet rock on the top plate.

followTheSound.title: Plate Vibration
followTheSound.explanation: Top plate vibrates in complex eigenmodes driven by bass bar and sound post.

followTheSound.title: Air Radiation
followTheSound.explanation: F-holes release Helmholtz resonance, boosting bass frequencies into the room.

followTheSound.title: Full-Body Radiation
followTheSound.explanation: Back plate and air cavity radiate the full tonal spectrum outward.
